attribution.note: Marcus's own prediction, listed under 'High confidence' in his own 2025 predictions post.

semantics.note: An unhedged 'will' under high confidence, so it is a scored forecast. The single-system qualifier, the more-than-4 threshold and the end-2025 horizon are all kept. The hedged second sentence is correctly left out.

contract.note: The criteria use the bet's own tasks and threshold, and they require an independent assessment rather than Marcus's own grading. There is no official panel score, but the margin is wide enough that this does not decide the result.

evidence.note: An independent year-end review graded this exact prediction correct. It found AI could at most perhaps do the reading-comprehension task.
The market resolved NO, but its creator followed Marcus's own appraisal, so it is not an independent finding.
These are March 2026 results, after the horizon, and they bear on only the video-game task. Context only.

reviews.rationale: The deadline (end of 2025) has passed. An independent year-end review found no system did more than about one task, well short of five. The packet contains no counterevidence that any system did five or more. The market resolution and the 2026 benchmark are context only.

attribution.note: Marcus's own parenthetical, attached to his high-confidence AGI prediction.

semantics.note: 'Will continue' under high confidence is an unhedged forecast. The 2025 horizon comes from the surrounding 'this year'. The normalised wording is faithful to the statement.

contract.note: Marcus named no measure, so the plain reading applies: prominent 2025 economic or financial framings of AGI, or moves to loosen the term. That is an ordinary reading. Whether a given framing counts as a 'game' is a judgment call, as the contract itself flags.

evidence.note: In February 2025 Microsoft's CEO dismissed AGI milestones and named 10% world growth as the real benchmark. That is an economic rather than scientific framing.
An August 2025 report covers Altman's retreat from AGI language, the fight over the contract's AGI clause, and an internal debate over whether a paper could complicate declaring AGI.

Published April 2026, before the evaluation date. It shows the profit-based contractual AGI definition stayed in force through 2025 and was kept in the October 2025 deal. Mostly background persistence, so context.

reviews.rationale: 2025 has ended. Dated 2025 reporting shows Microsoft's CEO recasting the AGI benchmark as economic growth, and OpenAI and Microsoft manoeuvring over a commercially defined AGI clause. Both fit the contract's plain reading. There is no counterevidence. The 'games' label is evaluative, but the financial framing clearly happened.
